aircraft._commentFlaps: No aircraft-specific flap detents are configured; use physical flap angle or raw handle percent pending in-sim handle-index verification.

aircraftCfg._comment: Use aircraft.cfg only when B38M is paired with an exact canonical or Microsoft/Asobo-qualified MAX 8 title and an exact first-party creator. B38M alone is intentionally insufficient. Optional traffic/selectability fields are not required because Microsoft permits them to be omitted.

lvars._comment: The cited Microsoft and Asobo sources do not define a 737 MAX 8 external LVAR, B-var, input-event, or hardware-integration map. Active telemetry stays on standard SimConnect data.

controls._comment: The exact-profile trusted adapter exposes 44 guarded actions backed by 34 Microsoft-documented MSFS 2024 standard events and 24 confirmation fields over 44 standard-SimVar fields. OFF/ON intents require fresh standard readback; four MCP targets are bounded; every unsatisfied route dispatches at most once without retry and requires newer matching or changed readback. Generic fallback remains disabled and the narrow standard gear/flap fallback stays enabled. These are generic simulator semantics, not a Boeing CMD A/B, MCP selector, or proprietary autothrottle contract. Spoilers, runway turnoff, vendor-private interfaces, and deep systems remain write-disabled.

meta.notes: Dedicated exact-profile page for the Microsoft / Asobo Studio Boeing 737 MAX 8 included with MSFS 2024. The trusted adapter exposes 44 standard-SimVar fields, 44 guarded actions, 24 confirmation fields, and 34 unique Microsoft-documented standard events with zero custom subscriptions. It prioritizes generic flight guidance and MCP targets, seven exterior-light outputs, gear, relative flap steps, and parking brake. Every action remains untested pending live MSFS 2024 validation.

knownIssues: The exact SimConnect TITLE and package/runtime paths have not been captured in-sim. The Asobo_B737_MAX8 SimObject segment and asobo-aircraft-b737max8 package segments are provisional identity hints based on existing runtime conventions; the cited public sources do not publish those identifiers.
The Microsoft Flight Simulator aircraft manuals page does not list a 737 MAX 8 manual.

The 44 standard-SimVar fields, 44 actions, and 24 confirmation fields remain untested against the live MSFS 2024 737 MAX 8; a documented standard event can still be ignored or incompletely mirrored by a complex aircraft.
AUTOPILOT_ON and AUTOPILOT_OFF expose only generic simulator master behavior. They cannot select or independently confirm Boeing CMD A versus CMD B.
Flight-director and autothrottle-arm OFF/ON intents share documented toggle events behind fresh readback. Standard state may still differ from the aircraft's internal annunciation or switch state.

Standard mode and target events do not reproduce proprietary Boeing MCP or autothrottle semantics. NAV hold is only a generic standard-state contract, and VNAV remains excluded; generic flight-level change is not asserted to reproduce every Boeing LVL CHG transition.
Exterior-light actions confirm seven standard lamp outputs only. Runway-turnoff writes and Boeing multi-position or split-light switch semantics remain excluded.
Spoiler state remains read-only; no spoiler, raw-axis, vendor-private, macro, engine, or deep-system writes are enabled.
The cited sources do not define a 737 MAX 8 LVAR, B-var, InputEvent, or hardware-integration map, and the adapter subscribes to zero custom variables.
Flap handle indexes are not confirmed, so this profile intentionally defines no local flap notch table.
All active write routes retain untested verification until the included MSFS 2024 aircraft is validated live.
